transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Could you tell me what’s been bringing you here today?

I guess… I came in because I don’t really trust myself anymore. Not in a dramatic way, I mean—well, it feels dramatic to say it out loud—but I keep thinking about this near-miss that happened, and I can’t stop turning it over in my head like it proves something awful about me. Like it proves I’m not safe, or I’m not meant to be a nurse, or I was stupid to think I could do this.

And it’s not just feeling bad about making a mistake. It’s more like… I feel like I’m a danger and a disappointment. Like everyone who believed in me was wrong. I keep thinking people would be better off if I wasn’t there, like if I just wasn’t involved, I couldn’t mess anything up. I know that probably sounds extreme, but it feels so true in my head that I can’t get away from it.
Can you tell me if these feelings have been present most days, and if so, how long have they been going on?

Yeah… most days. I mean, it’s not like every single minute is exactly the same, but it’s been there in some form almost all the time.

If I’m trying to place when it really started, it was after I graduated high school and started taking college classes and working full-time at the clinic. So… about a year and two months now, I think. It kind of crept in at first, like I thought I was just overwhelmed or adjusting, but it didn’t really go away. It’s been long enough that I don’t really remember what it felt like to not have this hanging over me most days.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things anymore, or that activities you used to enjoy don’t feel the same?

Yeah. I’ve noticed that a lot, actually.

I used to have these little things that made me feel like I could reset myself after class or after being at the clinic all day. Like I’d go jogging, even just around the neighborhood, and it would help clear my head. Or I’d knit while watching something, or I’d cook something kind of involved just because it felt nice to make something. I used to read after class too, even when I was tired.

Now it’s like… I come home still in my scrubs and I just sit on my bed. I’ll think, “I should go for a run,” or “I could make food,” or “I should at least pick up my book,” but I just don’t care. Not in the way I used to. It all feels like too much effort, or like there’s no point because it won’t make me feel better anyway. Sometimes I’ll just sit there for a long time, still dressed from the day, and I can’t make myself want any of it.
Have you noticed that you’ve been feeling more tired or that you don’t have the same energy as you used to, even when you’re not doing much?

I’m… not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I feel worn down a lot, but I don’t know if it’s the kind of tired you mean, or if it’s just from work and school and everything being… a lot.

Some days I do feel like I’m moving slower, like everything takes more effort than it should, but I also don’t really have a clean comparison anymore. Like, I can’t tell if I’m actually more tired than before or if I’m just noticing it more because I’m not doing as much. I haven’t been tracking it or anything.

I guess I wouldn’t say there’s one clear thing like, “Oh, I sleep and wake up exhausted every day,” or something like that. It’s more that I feel kind of drained in general, but I don’t know if that’s energy exactly. Does that make sense?
Can you tell me if there’s been any activity or thing you do, even a small one, that still feels meaningful or enjoyable to you most days?

Honestly… not really most days. I keep trying to think of something, because it feels bad to say “nothing,” like that sounds dramatic, but I can’t think of much that actually feels meaningful or enjoyable in the way it used to.

Before, I had these little routines that actually helped me feel like a person again after class or work. I’d go jogging to clear my head, or I’d knit while watching something, or cook something that took effort just because it felt satisfying. Sometimes I’d read after class even if I was tired, and it still felt like something I wanted.

Now I’ll come home in my scrubs and just sit on my bed, and I’ll think about doing those things, but it’s like there’s no pull toward them. I can’t make myself care. It’s not even that I hate them now… it’s more like they’re behind glass or something. I know I used to enjoy them, but I don’t feel connected to that anymore. Most days I just sit there and don’t end up doing any of it.
Have you been blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling guilty about things you don’t think you should feel guilty about?

Yeah… definitely. That’s honestly a big part of why I came in.

I keep blaming myself over this one thing that happened at work — it was a near-miss, and I know, technically, it didn’t become something worse, but I can’t stop replaying it. It feels like proof that I’m not meant to be a nurse, or that I’m dangerous somehow. Like even if other people would say, “You caught it,” or “It happens,” my brain doesn’t accept that. It just goes straight to, “You almost hurt someone. You shouldn’t be trusted.”

And then it kind of spreads from there. It’s not just guilt about the specific situation, it turns into this bigger thing where I feel like I’m a disappointment in general. Like to my patients, to people teaching me, to anyone who thought I could do this. I keep thinking everyone would be better off if I wasn’t there, because then I couldn’t mess anything up or let anyone down.

I know that might sound extreme, because nothing actually happened in the end, but I can’t make it feel that way. It feels like this one moment says something about who I am. Like it proves something bad about me.
Have you noticed that you've completely lost interest in all activities, to the point where nothing at all feels rewarding or worth doing?

Yeah… I think that’s pretty close to what it feels like. I don’t know if I’d say “completely” in some absolute way, because I can still recognize that those things are supposed to be good for me or that I used to like them, but they don’t feel rewarding anymore.

Like I used to go jogging to clear my head, and it actually helped — not even in a dramatic way, just like I could breathe again after class. Or I’d knit for a while, or cook something that took more than two minutes, or read after class because I wanted to. Those were all things that made the day feel… less flat, I guess.

Now I’ll get home still in my scrubs and just sit on my bed, and I’ll think, “I should go for a run,” or “I could pick up the knitting,” or “I should make real food,” but there’s just no feeling behind it. It’s like I can’t make myself care enough to start, and even imagining doing it doesn’t feel like it would be worth the effort. So I just sit there, and time passes, and nothing really feels like something I want.
